title: Check yourself: Streaming events and assembling a message

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A handler adds up the output token count of every `message_delta` it receives and reports three times the real cost. What does the page say it should do instead?

options.text: Overwrite the earlier figure, since each event restates the running tally
options.says: The page says "The output count in message_delta is cumulative: replace the stored one, do not add to it".

options.text: Take the input count from the final event and the output count from the first
options.says: Ruled out because "the output count comes from the last message_delta" and the input count from `message_start`.

options.text: Sum them all and then subtract the figure that the opening event gave
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "do not add to it".

options.text: Drop the field and measure the pieces of text that arrived in the stream
options.says: Ruled out because usage is read from the events: "Input tokens come from message_start".

questions.stem: A stream breaks in the middle of the fragments of a tool call's input. What should the code do?

options.text: Join the fragments received so far and parse them as the input
options.says: Ruled out because the fragments "are not valid JSON until the block ends".

options.text: Run the tool with whatever the first fragment held
options.says: Ruled out because "A fragment of tool input is a piece of text, not an object".

options.text: Throw the piece away and report the whole message as failed
options.says: The page says "Raise, so that the caller can decide" when a stream just stopped, because it "is an incomplete message, not a short one".

options.text: Keep the block and mark the message as a short one
options.says: Ruled out because the page says "an incomplete message, not a short one".
